name: The Podbielski Oak

location.address: Olympischer Platz 3, behind the Preussenturm at the Osttor (East Gate), Olympiastadion Berlin, 14053 Berlin

access: Free to view from outside the stadium fence at the Osttor (East Gate); stadium entry (paid, roughly EUR 7) lets visitors stand beside it. Public forecourt area, no appointment needed.
transport: U2 Olympia-Stadion, about 500m / 6 minute walk to the Osttor (East Gate)
verify_notes: Register (berlin-naturdenkmale.json, 4-6/B, 'Trauben-Eiche - Winter-Eiche', Quercus petraea, 'Olympia-Stadion, Haupteingang', designated 1993-03-02, 52.515037/13.242585) confirms designation and coordinates; the de.wikipedia Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf Naturdenkmal list gives the same tree at 52.51506/13.2426 with a Commons photo filename 'Westend Olympiastation Stieleiche.jpg' (Stieleiche = Quercus robur/pedunculate oak), an UNRESOLVED possible species conflict against the register's Quercus petraea, not run down further this pass. AGE/HISTORY DISPUTE between two independent sources, deliver both rather than pick a winner: (1) de.wikipedia's Olympiastadion (Berlin) article: 'Hinter dem Preussenturm am Osttor befindet sich die Podbielski-Eiche, ein etwa 200 Jahre altes geschuetztes Naturdenkmal, das seinen an Victor von Podbielski erinnernden Namen von einem gleichnamigen Baum des Vorgaengerstadions uebernahm' (about 200 years old, name 'inherited' from a like-named tree at the predecessor stadium, implying continuity). (2) golocal.de's Podbielski-Eiche entry: '1914 wurde aus Anlass des 70. Geburtstages des obersten deutschen Sportfunktionaers Victor v. Podbielski eine alte Eiche am Deutschen Stadion nach ihm benannt', then states explicitly that when the 1913 Deutsches Stadion was demolished to build the 1936 Olympiastadion, the ORIGINAL Podbielski-Eiche was FELLED and a replacement was planted in 1936 before the new stadium, carrying the same name; also states it is 'der einzige Baum auf dem 810m x 320m grossen Gelaende von Olympiastadion und Maifeld' (the only tree on the whole 810x320m stadium and Maifeld grounds), and that it survived WWII and the postwar period. If golocal.de is right, the living tree is a 1936 replanting, roughly 90 years old, not a 200-year-old original; if de.wikipedia's continuity framing is right, the tree could be older. Recording both rather than choosing. A WebSearch AI summary (not independently fetched, so NOT used as a source per the search-summary rule) also floated a girth of 4.50m via monumentaltrees.com, which 403'd to both curl and WebFetch this pass and has no Wayback snapshot for this specific tree page; girth left null rather than reported unverified. Either way this is a legitimate 'living replanting succeeding a felled original' case per the site's own Elm-of-Saint-Gervais precedent: the story should describe the LIVING tree standing today. Remarkable regardless of which age reading holds: the only tree on the entire Olympiastadion/Maifeld grounds, named in 1914 for sports official Victor von Podbielski, tied to both the 1913 Deutsches Stadion (originally intended for the cancelled 1916 Olympics) and the 1936 Nazi Olympics stadium that replaced it. Alive now: both sources describe it in the present tense as a current stadium landmark; the Commons photo (undated in what I could read) shows it standing at the East Gate.
